patch_description:
The current ansatz uses 11 distinct trainable parameters (8 individual per-qubit RY angles plus 3 shared RZ/entangling params), giving a strong worst-group margin (0.11) but a large train/val gap (0.24) and low parameter efficiency. Prior experiments show that reducing distinct-parameter count strongly increases the combined score even at some accuracy cost, and that entanglement depth can be increased "for free" by reusing the same shared parameter name on additional two-qubit gates (since the block is repeated with identical parameters).

This edit collapses the 8 independent per-qubit RY angles into a 2-parameter even/odd alternating scheme (capturing input-dependent structure while drastically cutting parameter count), keeps single shared RZ pre/post phase parameters, and replaces the single-ring CRZ entangling layer with two shared-parameter entangling layers: a nearest-neighbor ring (including wraparound 7-0) and a skip-2 connectivity layer, both reusing the same "ent" parameter. This increases circuit connectivity/expressivity (useful for separating the hardest validation groups) without adding any new trainable parameters, going from 11 distinct params down to 5, which should reduce overfitting/generalization gap and raise parameter efficiency while retaining reasonable margin.
